title: Firewater Pump Package

introduction.definition: A firewater pump package supplies water to sprinklers, hydrants and deluge systems. Typically a listed horizontal split-case pump driven by a diesel engine (or electric motor) is installed with a controller, a jockey pump that maintains system pressure, a relief valve and a test header. NFPA 20 governs the arrangement and performance.
applications: Alumina refineries and mineral processing plants
key_points: Built from: Horizontal Split Case Pump (module 2) or Vertical Turbine Pump (module 4)
Listed pumps: ≥150 % rated flow at ≥65 % rated pressure; shut-off ≤140 % (NFPA 20 — verify edition)
Jockey pump keeps the network pressurised
Weekly churn tests and annual flow tests

classification.configuration: Horizontal split-case fire pump + diesel engine driver + jockey pump + controllers

introduction.summary: A fire pump package is a complete, listed pumping system that must start automatically and deliver its rated flow and pressure to sprinklers and hydrants whenever system pressure falls. It combines a fire pump (here a horizontal split-case pump), a reliable driver (diesel engine with its own batteries, fuel and cooling from the pump discharge, or an electric motor), a fire pump controller, a small jockey pump that keeps the system pressurised against minor leaks, a main relief valve, a test header for flow testing, and isolation/check valves. Installation and acceptance are governed by fire codes such as NFPA 20.

parts.name: Lower Casing Half (with Nozzles & Feet)
parts.function: Lower half of the axially split casing: carries the suction and discharge nozzles, feet and bearing brackets, so the rotor can be removed without disturbing the piping.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, cast steel, bronze, duplex.

parts.name: Upper Casing Half (Removable)
parts.function: Removable top half of the casing; lifting it exposes the complete rotor for inspection.

parts.name: Double-Suction Impeller
parts.function: Double-suction impeller: liquid enters from both sides, halving eye velocity (lower NPSHr) and balancing axial thrust.

parts.name: Shaft & Sleeves
parts.function: Transmits torque from the coupling to the impeller(s).
parts.material: Carbon steel, 4140 alloy steel, 410/420 or 316 stainless, duplex.

parts.name: Mechanical Seal – Inboard
parts.function: Seals the rotating shaft where it leaves the pressurised casing.
parts.material: Faces: carbon-graphite, silicon carbide, tungsten carbide; metal parts stainless steel; elastomers per fluid.

parts.name: Bearing Housing – Inboard
parts.function: Holds the shaft bearings and oil or grease, and supports the overhung impeller.

parts.name: Radial Bearing – Inboard
parts.function: Carries radial load near the impeller end.

parts.name: Mechanical Seal – Outboard
parts.function: Seals the rotating shaft where it leaves the pressurised casing.
parts.material: Faces: carbon-graphite, silicon carbide, tungsten carbide; metal parts stainless steel; elastomers per fluid.

parts.name: Bearing Housing – Outboard
parts.function: Holds the shaft bearings and oil or grease, and supports the overhung impeller.

parts.name: Thrust Bearing – Outboard
parts.function: Carries axial hydraulic thrust and locates the shaft axially.
parts.material: Bearing steel; brass or polyamide cages.

parts.name: Suction & Discharge Piping
parts.function: Connects the pump to the system.
parts.material: Carbon steel, stainless steel, ductile iron, HDPE/PVC as appropriate.

parts.name: Suction Isolation, Discharge Check & Isolation Valves
parts.function: Isolation valve, fully open or fully closed.
parts.material: Cast iron, ductile iron, carbon or stainless steel.

parts.name: Suction & Discharge Pressure Gauges
parts.function: Indicates suction or discharge pressure for operation and performance checks.
parts.material: Stainless steel case and wetted parts.

parts.name: Drive Shaft (Cardan) between Pump and Engine
parts.function: Connects pump and engine while accommodating small misalignment.

parts.name: Drive Shaft Guard
parts.function: Prevents contact with rotating parts.
parts.material: Steel, aluminium or non-sparking brass for hazardous areas.

parts.name: Diesel Engine (Listed Fire-Pump Driver)
parts.function: Independent prime mover that runs even if electrical power fails.

parts.name: Crankshaft, Crank Throws & Flywheel
parts.function: Smooths engine torque and drives the pump.

parts.name: Pistons (6 Cylinders)
parts.function: Convert the pressure of the burning fuel–air charge into force on the crankshaft (four-stroke: intake, compression, power, exhaust).
parts.material: Aluminium alloy, steel crowns on heavy-duty engines.

parts.name: Connecting Rods
parts.function: Link each piston to its crank throw, turning straight-line motion into rotation.

parts.name: Heat Exchanger, Exhaust Silencer & Air Cleaner
parts.function: Engine cooling (heat exchanger fed from pump discharge), exhaust silencer and air cleaner.

parts.name: Starting Batteries (2 Sets)
parts.function: Two independent battery sets to start the engine.

parts.name: Diesel Day Tank on Stand
parts.function: Stores diesel for the required run time.

parts.name: Fire Pump Controller & Jockey Pump Controller
parts.function: Houses starters, protection and control logic for the pumps.
parts.material: Painted or stainless steel enclosure; IP rating per location.

parts.name: Jockey (Pressure Maintenance) Pump
parts.function: Keeps the fire main pressurised against small leaks so the main fire pump starts only on real demand.

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Frame & End Shields
parts.function: Encloses the stator and supports the bearings; feet or flange mount the motor to the baseplate or pump.
parts.material: Cast iron or aluminium frame; steel fasteners.

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Stator
parts.function: Produces the rotating magnetic field.
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Converts the rotating field into shaft torque (squirrel-cage induction rotor).
parts.material: Electrical steel, die-cast aluminium or copper.

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Bearings (DE & NDE)
parts.function: Support the motor rotor at drive and non-drive ends.

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Cooling Fan
parts.function: Draws cooling air over the finned frame.

parts.name: Vertical Motor – Fan Cover
parts.function: Guards the fan and directs air along the fins.

parts.name: Main Pressure Relief Valve
parts.function: Limits system pressure (required on engine-driven pumps where shut-off pressure could exceed system rating).

parts.name: Test Header with Hose Valves
parts.function: Allows flow testing of the pump through hose streams or a flow meter.

parts.name: Baseplate
parts.function: Provides a rigid common mounting for pump and driver, maintains alignment and transfers loads to the foundation.
parts.material: Carbon steel, painted; stainless steel for hygienic or corrosive areas.

foundation: Dedicated, fire-separated pump room; rigid baseplate.
alignment: Align pump and motor shafts with dial indicators or laser after grouting and again after connecting the piping (hot alignment check for hot service).
Target the coupling manufacturer's tolerances; typical practice for 1500–3000 rpm is ≤0.05 mm offset and ≤0.05 mm/100 mm angularity — verify.
Correct soft foot (< 0.05 mm) before final alignment.
piping: Suction from a reliable source (tank/reservoir); no throttling on suction.
Test header or flow meter loop; relief valve per standard.
commissioning: Acceptance test at churn, 100 % and 150 % flow.
Controller and engine start tests (both batteries).

periodic.task: Annual flow test at 0, 100, 150 % rated flow.

video_tutorials.title: Firewater Pump Package — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Firewater Pump Package.
Weekly churn test run.
Check batteries and fuel level.
Annual flow test at 0, 100, 150 % rated flow.
Inspect split-case pump internals.
Watch for engine fails to start: controller alarm. Common cause: batteries, fuel.
Watch for low flow at test: below curve. Common cause: impeller wear, suction blockage.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
